alt: Four strands of the topic, each with Urdu words: part-time work and work experience (جز وقتی ملازمت, کام کا تجربہ, گاہک), professions (ڈاکٹر, وکیل, صحافی), career choices (تنخواہ, ذمہ داری, محنتی) and ambitions (پیشہ, ہنر / مہارت, کاروبار).
caption: Work now, professions, what matters in a job, and ambitions; study routes belong to Topic 3.

alt: بننا means to become and بنانا means to make. میں ڈاکٹر بننا چاہتا ہوں and میں صحافی بننا چاہتی ہوں are correct; میں ڈاکٹر بنانا چاہتا ہوں means "I want to make a doctor". An ambition then needs a reason with کیونکہ.
caption: بننا چاہنا for an ambition, with چاہتا or چاہتی to match the speaker, plus a reason.

alt: Four Urdu sentences: a present routine in an uncle’s shop, one past work-experience event with میں نے, repeated past tasks in the habitual past without نے (وہاں میں فون سنتی تھی), and a condition about becoming a doctor. میں نے فون سنتی تھی is wrong.
caption: Use نے for one completed transitive event, never for the habitual past.

after: ## Worked example 1: part-time work and an ambition
alt: Four moves in the model answer, each with its Urdu frame: a present routine with جہاں, what was learned (اس کام سے میں نے سیکھا ہے کہ), an ambition with a reason (صحافی بننا چاہتا ہوں کیونکہ), and a priority comparison (سے زیادہ اہم یہ ہے کہ).
caption: Routine, lesson learned, justified ambition, considered priority.

after: ## Worked example 3: a short reading question
alt: The reading text split into clauses: a fact (she works in a bank), the advantage (good pay), the disadvantage after لیکن (the work is boring), what she does now after اس لیے (cooking classes, a trap) and the ambition (her own restaurant one day).
caption: Separate what someone does now from what they hope to do.
